A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical work. Their complete main texts, algorithms, equations and proof appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and appendix reordering.

before.justification: V1 presents algorithms, regret guarantees and mathematical proofs, including its appendices, without original experimental, simulation or data-analysis results.

after.justification: V2 remains entirely theoretical. Its added arguments and revised proofs do not include original empirical results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 5 now computes and sends G xi_{t+1} at round t, replacing G xi_t in v1. This corrects the movement coefficient used for the next update. The underlying mirror-descent, aggregation and batching procedures are retained.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets for training or evaluation. Movement costs, delayed feedback and time-varying memory remain theoretical application settings.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline experiments. Comparisons with earlier algorithms concern theoretical guarantees.

E3.justification: Neither version contains empirical evaluation protocols, data splits, experimental metrics or evaluation budgets.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, robustness tests, error analyses or empirical case studies. The added comparison between regret bounds is a mathematical argument.

E5.justification: Repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates and statistical tests are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: No empirical measurements or observed findings are added, removed or updated. Changes to theoretical guarantees and derivations are covered under T1.

T1.justification: V2 changes the path-length convention to exclude initial displacement and standardizes the logarithmic factor as P_T[1+log(1+4MT^2/epsilon)]. It repairs movement-cost accounting in Lemma B.2 and Theorem 4.1, corrects the memory-proof linearization, and handles endpoint cases. New Proposition B.3 proves the comparison between existing bounds, and Section 5.2 adds a memory lower-bound argument. These refine the retained theoretical framework and leading rates.

C1.justification: The abstract changes its comparator factor from 1+P_T to M^2+M P_T, making explicit the norm dependence already present in v1's main analysis. The conclusion changes per-round complexity from O(log T) to O(d log T). The principal novelty claims and two applications remain.

C2.justification: Remark 4.3 explains why the first-order bound is never worse up to constants, accounting for the movement-coefficient index shift. Section 5.2 newly argues that fixed-memory dependence is minimax optimal. Section 2 removes v1's blanket assertion that the comparator movement term is lower order.

D1.justification: Corollary 5.3 explicitly specifies the combined coefficient G|m_{t+1}|+lambda_{t+1}. Appendix B clarifies that the learning-rate grid uses the original horizon T because the epoch count is unknown. The conclusion also makes the dimensional runtime factor explicit.

R1.justification: V2 adds Kumar et al. (2023), Ryabchenko et al. (2025) and Yang et al. (2025), extending positioning around memory lower bounds and delayed learning. The related-work attribution for dynamic regret with memory changes from Wan et al. (2024) to Zhao et al. (2023).

P1.justification: V2 edits explanatory prose and notation, makes Contributions unnumbered, moves auxiliary lemmas from Appendix A to Appendix D, and updates author order, affiliations and acknowledgments. It adds an Impact Statement. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column presentation to a two-column conference layout, with redesigned title and author blocks, running headers, equation wrapping and relocated column-width algorithm boxes. The appendices retain a full-width layout. No empirical figures or tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: V2 improves technical precision through Algorithm 5's indexing correction, repaired movement accounting in the Theorem 4.1 proof, and more accurate abstract and runtime statements. Proposition B.3 supplies additional justification for the bound comparison. Theorem 3.1 uses a coarser logarithmic path-length factor, but the leading rates and detailed base guarantee remain. These support a limited overall improvement.
